thread.title: Parks officials propose timber sale for health of Lewis Emery Park - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Parks officials propose timber sale for health of Lewis Emery Park - NewsBreak

author: Corey J. Murray
title: Parks officials propose timber sale for health of Lewis Emery Park - NewsBreak
text:
By Corey J. Murray ,
19 hours ago HILLSDALE — Trustees on the Hillsdale County Parks Commission are considering harvesting select lumber from Lewis Emery Park as part of an effort to better manage the 96‑acre property and promote long-term forest health.
Parks Manager Mike Wertz briefed the Hillsdale County Board on Jan. 13, informing officials that trustees have already solicited bids. The proposed work could generate roughly $40,000 in revenue from the sale of timber, and would cost the greater municipality nothing.
Wertz stressed the goal, however, is stewardship — not profit.
“This isn't a money grab,” he said.
If the project moves forward, the proceeds could be used for pond weed control and community center roof replacement at Lewis Emery Park.
Brent Leininger, chair of the Hillsdale County Finance Committee, cautioned that deed restrictions might limit timber harvesting. The land was gifted by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources in the 1960s for use as a public park.
Leininger said he'd provide a copy of the deed to attorney Tom Thompson for review and report back before the trustees’ next meeting Jan. 22.
More: $345,300 in improvements planned for 96-acre Lewis Emery Park
Commissioner Brad Benzing noted any revenue from the sale would still be subject to county policy. Trustees would need to file a budget amendment and appropriation request, and the money would initially be deposited into the general fund.
Leininger added he hopes the county’s capital improvement fund will have enough money remaining this year to cover the community center roof replacement, regardless of the lumber proposal.
Maintenance projects at county-owned parks have largely stalled over the years due to limited funding. Hillsdale County allocates just over $40,000 annually for all five parks — an amount trustees say is roughly equivalent to funding levels three decades years ago and doesn't account for inflation .
More: Parks appropriation inadequate to maintain five county parks
In 2025, Leininger sought a $1.7 million state appropriation for pond dredging, roof replacement and repaving at Lewis Emery Park, but the request failed.
The county did secure a $255,000 grant through the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund to improve the park's trails and docks for ADA compliance, with $89,800 committed in local match funds. The project is expected to begin this year and be completed by 2028.
